turns: Which product categories have total revenue above Rs 20,000?

turns: Which 5 customers have spent the most?
reference_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity) AS s FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name FROM t JOIN customers c ON c.id = t.customer_id ORDER BY t.s DESC LIMIT 5

turns: Which city has the most customers?
reference_sql: SELECT city FROM customers GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers GROUP BY city))

turns: What share of total revenue does each product category contribute?
reference_sql: SELECT p.category, 100.0 * SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity) / (SELECT SUM(i2.unit_price * i2.quantity) FROM order_items i2 JOIN orders o2 ON o2.id = i2.order_id WHERE o2.status != 'cancelled') FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.category
note: percentages; the grader compares with a numeric tolerance; v2: alternate accepts fractions (representation only)
alt_reference_sql: SELECT p.category, 1.0 * SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity) / (SELECT SUM(i2.unit_price * i2.quantity) FROM order_items i2 JOIN orders o2 ON o2.id = i2.order_id WHERE o2.status != 'cancelled') FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.category

turns: For each customer, show their total spend and their rank by spend.
reference_sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity), RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity) DESC) FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.id

turns: Which customers spent more than the average customer?
reference_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity) AS s FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name FROM t JOIN customers c ON c.id = t.customer_id WHERE t.s > (SELECT AVG(s) FROM t)
